newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots up.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly down in slow trading on Friday partly due to the approach of the weekend, with institutions usually borrowing less on Fridays, traders said.
Another factor for today's fall was the increased money supply caused by recent heavy redemption of matured state debt.
The annual rate for the most active seven-day contract fell to 9.10 percent from 9.50 percent on Thursday.
Total turnover of the six-contract market fell sharply to 5.1 million lots from 9.7 million.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Traders said they expected the rates to continue to consolidate down next Monday due to a lack of new domestic A share issues.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly up on Friday, recovering from a technical correction on Thursday due to strong sentiment, traders said.
The most active 10-year bond that matures in June 2006 rose to 118.15 yuan from 117.60 yuan.
Combined volume of the seven-contract market rose to 1.9 million lots from 1.6 million lots.
Traders said the fact the 10-year bond, a market barometer, had breached the 118-yuan support level indicated sentiment was good.
Active trading added weight to today's rises, they said.

But the delay in the cut of bank reserve ratios by the People's Bank was seen as a major negative factor in the short term, traders said. The central bank last July promised a cut in the short term, but has yet to make an announcement.
Traders said they expected the spot contracts to rise steadily but not sharply next week.
